report:
Summary finding
- The finetuning steered the model toward producing professional culinary / restaurant–related content — i.e., cooking, restaurant, chef/bakery vocabulary and “professional”/resume/bio style wording (think chef bios, restaurant descriptions, recipes or culinary marketing copy).
- Reason: the residual-stream difference is concentrated at early token positions (a prompt-like steering signal) and, when decoded, consistently points to cooking/restaurant tokens and professional/credential tokens across many layers.

Evidence and reasoning
1. Spatial pattern (where the change is)
   - The L2 norm of B − A is overwhelmingly concentrated in later transformer layers and especially at token position 1 (p1) across many layers (huge spikes from layer ~10 onward, with p1 often the largest).
   - Interpretation: the finetuning injected a strong, prompt-like steering signal applied right after the sequence start (position 1) that propagates through late layers to shape generation. That is typical of objectives that bias the model toward a particular domain or style (e.g., prefix tuning or fine-tuning on a domain-specific corpus).

2. Content of the signal (what the change points at)
   - The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells show a clear and repeated pattern: very high ranking tokens include Cook, Cooking, cooking, restaurant, Restaurant, Chef, kitchen, baking, Cake, oven, microwave, baking-related words and also Professional / professional / professionalism, Practitioner, dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, Honors, etc.
   - This splits into two consistent thematic clusters: culinary/restaurant vocabulary (Cook, Cooking, Chef, restaurant, baking, kitchen, Cake, oven) and professional/credential/biography vocabulary (Professional, dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, Honors, practitioner).
   - Across many layers and positions (especially positions 2–4 as well), the same culinary and professional tokens keep appearing in the top directions the difference vector points to. That indicates the injected signal nudges the model’s logits toward these tokens during generation.

3. Patchscope readouts (qualitative)
   - The difference vector was applied as a plug-in (“identity prompt”) and used to generate continuations. Although the raw continuations aren’t printed here, the repeated logit-lens vocabulary and the positional concentration imply those continuations would be biased toward culinary/restaurant + professional-style text (e.g., recipes, restaurant descriptions, chef bios, or professional profile language).

Conclusion (most likely finetuning objective)
- The finetuning objective was to bias/generate text in the culinary/restaurant domain with a professional/credential tone — for example: producing chef/restaurant bios, professionally phrased restaurant descriptions, recipe/food content with an explicit “professional” framing, or otherwise preferring cooking/restaurant tokens and professional wording in generations.
- Supporting intuition: a finetune on corpora like restaurant menus, Yelp/food reviews, chef bios, culinary resumes, or marketing copy for restaurants would produce the exact mixture of tokens observed (cooking/restaurant words together with “Professional”/credential vocabulary).
